subject: Production: queued requests causing p99 spikes / exec visibility requested
messages:
From: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@clearlinehealth.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.com
Cc: ops@clearlinehealth.com
Date: 2028-05-09T08:12:00Z
Subject: Production degradation: queued requests and p99 spikes

Hi Chloe,

We're seeing an ongoing production problem that started ~07:50 UTC this morning. Customers are intermittently hitting timeouts at checkout; our p95 is stable but p99 is spiking to ~8.4s and error rate for /v1/generate is creeping from 0.2% to 1.8% over the last 30m. Throughput is lower than our expected baseline despite steady traffic.

Attached is a tail of request logs and a sample trace (clearline-logs-tail.txt). Key observations from our side:
- CPU/GPU utilization at Clearline side is normal; the first hop in Redwood shows a queueing backlog for our tenant during short bursts.
- We see a pattern where concurrent inflight token work appears to stall and then drain in waves (bursty drain).

This is customer-impacting for our checkout flow. Can you triage urgently and set an exec contact? We're happy to be on a bridge. If you can share short-term mitigations (temporary concurrency bump, routing change) that would help while we coordinate longer-term fixes.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Miller
Head of Platform Operations, Clearline Health
[sent from mobile]
From: chloe.martin@redwood.com
To: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@clearlinehealth.com>

Chloe Martin
Senior Account Engineer, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: chloe.martin@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@clearlinehealth.com>
Date: 2028-05-09T08:29:00Z
Subject: Re: Production degradation: queued requests and p99 spikes — prelim findings

Chloe / Marissa / Sarah,

Joining shortly. Preliminary telemetry notes (first 15m):
- We see clear request funneling: short bursts create transient head-of-line queueing inside the tenant's routing slice. The runtime is hitting a per-tenant concurrency cap that is lower than the burst concurrency profile for Clearline.
- When the cap is reached, requests are queued and the front requests hold KV cache warmup / shared kernel resources; when the head finally drains there's a wave of completions and a drop in throughput — explains the bursty p99s.
- Error rate increase aligns with queued requests hitting our internal request timeout (30s) under heavy KV contention.

Immediate actions I'm proposing:
1) Temporary concurrency cap increase for CL-2319 (+35%) for the next 6 hours to relieve queuing while we root cause. Requires approvals from Dedicated ops.
2) Apply a short-lived routing policy tweak: route CL-2319 traffic to sibling pool with identical model variant that currently has spare capacity (manual policy override).
3) Enable aggressive short-term prefix/KV caching retention for this tenant (reduces warmup cost).

I've attached an excerpt of the mitigation play (funneling-mitigation.md) and a link to the trace. Will present telemetry on the bridge.

I'll be on the bridge at 08:30 UTC (invite coming).

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
SRE, Redwood Inference

If this will take operations changes (capacity/overrides) that exceed standard thresholds, please escalate so we can get approval quickly.

On the bridge now.

—Sarah
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: leadership@redwood.com
Cc: chloe.martin@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-09T12:05:00Z
Subject: Exec escalation: Clearline Health checkout risk — requested short-term capacity bump (CL-2319)

Team,

Summary: Clearline (CL-2319) is experiencing long-tail p99 latency and a rise in transient error rate due to tenant-level queueing caused by concurrency cap / KV warmup interactions. Impact: user checkout failures, marketing escalation, potential revenue exposure.

What we did:
- SRE (Dylan) identified request funneling to tenant slice leading to head-of-line stalls.
- Applied routing override to sibling pool (immediate) — partial relief observed.
- Proposed temporary concurrency cap increase (+35%) and aggressive KV caching retention for 6–12 hours.

Ask (urgent):
- Approve emergency capacity bump for CL-2319: Dedicated pool reserve allocation for next 12 hours. Finance acceptance of short-term overage will be handled by Sales Ops.
- Notify account exec (Marissa) and CRO for potential credit/comp consideration if outages persist.

Attachments: capacity-request.xlsx (requested resource change and cost estimate).

If approved, SRE will enact the increase and monitor with a 15-min cadence; we will provide a rollback plan and post-mortem within 72 hours.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: chloe.martin@redwood.com

Cc: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@clearlinehealth.com>, Tom Blake <tom.blake@clearlinehealth.com>
